hypotheses.title: Sulindac Extends Lifespan in Mus musculus
hypotheses.claim: Administration of sulindac extends lifespan in Mus musculus. Treated mice are expected to show a measurable increase in median and maximal lifespan relative to untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Sulindac modulates inflammatory and prostaglandin signaling, and reduced inflammatory tone is a recognized contributor to slower aging and prolonged survival in mammals.
hypotheses.prediction: Mice receiving sulindac will exhibit significantly longer median and maximal lifespans than vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a sufficiently powered cohort of mice to sulindac or vehicle treatment and follow them until natural death, comparing lifespan distributions between groups.

hypotheses.title: Medium-Chain Triglyceride Oil Extends Lifespan in Mus musculus
hypotheses.claim: Dietary supplementation with medium-chain triglyceride oil extends lifespan in Mus musculus. Supplemented mice are expected to live longer than mice receiving an isocaloric control oil.
hypotheses.rationale: Medium-chain triglycerides alter energy metabolism and ketone body availability, and improved metabolic flexibility is plausibly linked to delayed aging and extended survival in mammals.
hypotheses.prediction: Mice fed medium-chain triglyceride oil will show significantly greater median and maximal lifespans than isocaloric controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Assign large cohorts of mice to diets supplemented with medium-chain triglyceride oil or an isocaloric control oil and record lifespan until all animals have died.

hypotheses.title: Early Nordihydroguaiaretic Acid Treatment Extends Lifespan in Mus musculus
hypotheses.claim: Nordihydroguaiaretic acid extends lifespan in young Mus musculus when started before weaning. Early-treated mice are expected to outlive untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Intervening before weaning acts during a developmental window when metabolic and growth pathways are being set, so early modulation of lipoxygenase activity could produce durable changes that slow aging.
hypotheses.prediction: Mice treated with nordihydroguaiaretic acid before weaning will display significantly longer lifespans than untreated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Begin nordihydroguaiaretic acid administration in pre-weaning pups and matched untreated controls, then rear both groups identically and compare lifespan distributions.

hypotheses.title: Sulindac Extends Lifespan via Insulin/IGF-1 Signaling
hypotheses.claim: Sulindac extends lifespan in Mus musculus through activation of the insulin/IGF-1 signaling pathway. The lifespan benefit of sulindac is expected to depend on this pathway's activity.
hypotheses.rationale: The insulin/IGF-1 signaling pathway is a central regulator of aging in mammals, and its modulation can alter stress resistance, metabolism, and longevity, providing a mechanistic route by which sulindac could extend lifespan.
hypotheses.prediction: Sulindac-treated mice will show altered insulin/IGF-1 pathway activity, and the lifespan extension will be abolished when the pathway's activity is prevented.
hypotheses.experiment: Treat mice with sulindac or vehicle in the presence and absence of genetic or pharmacological blockade of insulin/IGF-1 signaling, then compare lifespans across all four groups.

hypotheses.title: Dimethyl Fumarate Extends Lifespan in Mus musculus
hypotheses.claim: Administration of dimethyl fumarate extends lifespan in Mus musculus. Treated mice are expected to show increased median and maximal lifespan relative to vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Dimethyl fumarate activates the Nrf2 antioxidant response, and enhanced cellular defense against oxidative stress is a biologically plausible route to slower aging and longer survival in mammals.
hypotheses.prediction: Mice receiving dimethyl fumarate will exhibit significantly longer median and maximal lifespans than vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize mice to dimethyl fumarate or vehicle treatment, maintain both groups under identical conditions, and compare lifespan distributions until all animals have died.

hypotheses.title: Acetaminophen Extends Lifespan in Mus musculus
hypotheses.claim: Administration of acetaminophen extends lifespan in Mus musculus. Treated mice are expected to live significantly longer than vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Acetaminophen influences inflammatory signaling and cellular stress responses, and mild modulation of these processes is a recognized potential mechanism for extending mammalian lifespan.
hypotheses.prediction: Mice treated with acetaminophen will show significantly greater median and maximal lifespans than vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Assign a sufficiently powered cohort of mice to acetaminophen or vehicle and record survival until natural death, comparing lifespan distributions between groups.

hypotheses.title: Nordihydroguaiaretic Acid Extends Lifespan in Mus musculus
hypotheses.claim: Administration of nordihydroguaiaretic acid extends lifespan in Mus musculus. Treated mice are expected to show increased median and maximal lifespan relative to untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Nordihydroguaiaretic acid inhibits lipoxygenase activity and reduces lipid peroxidation, and diminished oxidative lipid damage is a biologically plausible contributor to delayed aging and longer survival in mammals.
hypotheses.prediction: Mice receiving nordihydroguaiaretic acid will exhibit significantly longer median and maximal lifespans than untreated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize mice to nordihydroguaiaretic acid or control treatment, rear both groups identically, and compare lifespan distributions until all animals have died.

hypotheses.title: Sulindac Shortens Lifespan in Mus musculus
hypotheses.claim: Administration of sulindac shortens lifespan in Mus musculus. Treated mice are expected to show reduced median and maximal lifespan relative to vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Sulindac inhibits prostaglandin synthesis broadly, and sustained disruption of prostaglandin-dependent tissue maintenance and repair processes could impose physiological costs that accelerate aging in mammals.
hypotheses.prediction: Mice receiving sulindac will exhibit significantly shorter median and maximal lifespans than vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a sufficiently powered cohort of mice to sulindac or vehicle treatment and follow them until natural death, comparing lifespan distributions between groups.

hypotheses.title: Nordihydroguaiaretic Acid Shortens Lifespan in Mus musculus
hypotheses.claim: Administration of nordihydroguaiaretic acid shortens lifespan in Mus musculus. Treated mice are expected to show reduced median and maximal lifespan relative to untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Nordihydroguaiaretic acid broadly suppresses lipoxygenase-derived mediators involved in tissue homeostasis, and chronic disruption of these signaling functions could accumulate damage that accelerates aging in mammals.
hypotheses.prediction: Mice treated with nordihydroguaiaretic acid will show significantly shorter median and maximal lifespans than untreated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Assign large cohorts of mice to nordihydroguaiaretic acid or control treatment, maintain both groups identically, and compare lifespan distributions until all animals have died.

hypotheses.title: Nicotinamide Extends Lifespan in Mus musculus
hypotheses.claim: Administration of nicotinamide extends lifespan in Mus musculus. Treated mice are expected to show increased median and maximal lifespan relative to vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Nicotinamide is a precursor of NAD+, and maintaining NAD+-dependent sirtuin and energy metabolism pathways is a biologically plausible route to slower aging and extended survival in mammals.
hypotheses.prediction: Mice receiving nicotinamide will exhibit significantly longer median and maximal lifespans than vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize mice to nicotinamide or vehicle treatment, rear both groups under identical conditions, and record survival until natural death for comparison of lifespan distributions.
